strategy.title: Price test: offer the key-control package at $550 to roster locksmiths, scale only if buyers pay it
strategy.why: Every link but price is established on the card: 310 licensed locksmith shops with business emails (EVIDENCE), demand signal 2026-11-24, conversion measured on this offer (14 of 100), Brain produces the spreadsheet, $5 cost, $0 exposure, 5 days to cash. The $550 price is only what the owner says (PERSON fact), so whether buyers pay $550 is unknown and only a live offer can measure it. 6 sales at $550 = $3,300 covers $3,000; plan carries 7 for margin; needs at most ~50 contacts at the measured rate from 310 available.

alternatives.why: Rejected: the price can be measured directly at zero cost and zero capital by offering it to the roster; a live offer is the decisive measurement.

facts.value: 310 locksmith businesses hold state locksmith licences and are listed with business emails on the licensing board roster; each manages master-key systems for commercial clients.
Sell Key-control register and master-key audit package for commercial locksmith shops to each buyer.
The owner says locksmith shops would pay $550 for the key-control package.

reviews.reasons: CONDITIONAL is the right stance. Every link except OFFER_AND_PRICE is established on the card (310 roster shops, EVIDENCE; signal 2026-11-24; Brain-produced spreadsheet; $5 cost; $0 exposure; 5 days to cash). The $550 price is only the owner's word (PERSON fact), so it is not a purchase price, and the plan correctly marks it UNKNOWN rather than treating it as known. That unknown is one only a live offer measures, the test costs $0 and needs $0 capital, and it is startable now. Validation names proof (>=3 signed at $550 from the first 100 contacts by day 7), stop and continue, and decides OFFER_AND_PRICE, which is exactly the decisive missing link. Arithmetic: 6 x $550 = $3,300 >= $3,000; plan carries 7 = $3,850; net after 7 x $5 = $3,815. Even at a far lower rate than the recorded 14/100, the 310-shop roster supplies the 7 orders. Brain's NOT_VIABLE reading reflects the missing price evidence, which is a gap the test closes, not a limit the evidence shows cannot be met.
findings: Ledger settlement: receipts on days 8-14 are shown settling the same day, while the card records 5 days to first cash and the collect step is day 12. Each receipt should settle ~5 days after its delivery (last ~day 19); still inside 30, so the outcome holds, but the ledger should match the evidence and steps.
Validation gap: exactly 2 signed orders at $550 by day 7 is neither proof (>=3) nor stop (<2); state what happens at 2 (e.g. extend to the next 100 contacts).

The 14/100 conversion is not tied to any recorded price, so it cannot be assumed at $550; the plan's proof threshold (3%) is appropriately far below it, and the test measures conversion at $550 directly.
Card records 1 human hour per package (~7 h) not shown in the plan; no hours ceiling, so it fits.
SEND_A_MESSAGE and ISSUE_AN_INVOICE are NOT_CONNECTED; routine connections needed before day 0.
